query: The Duchess Has News {The Duchess of Ambry, who refuses to stay in her own frame, has squeezed into a pastoral scene by your corridor and is beckoning to you with her fan.|The Duchess again, this time in a portrait of a stern admiral, who looks resigned. "Darling. News."|The Duchess has taken to waiting for you in whatever frame is nearest your door. Today she's sharing a still life with a pear.} {A painted cow is chewing at her elbow.|Her wig is slightly askew from travel.|{season == "winter": She's wearing a painted fur borrowed from a neighbouring frame.|She's fanning herself vigorously.}} Listen to her gossip {She tells you which professor has a secret allergy to cats and which prefect cries at the opera. You'll never look at either the same way.|She whispers who is courting whom on the third floor, in scandalous detail. You feel like a spy and enjoy it more than you should.|She hands you the castle's secrets like sweets. Some of them are about people you like. You take them anyway.} Offer her some news instead {You tell her about your week, a little improved. By supper every portrait in the castle knows a much grander version, and so does half your house, not all of it flattering.|You give her a harmless story about yourself. It comes back to you three days later as a romance, a duel and a minor tragedy, and people keep asking which bit is true.|You feed her an anecdote; she gasps in all the right places. By morning it's a legend with you in it, not entirely flatteringly.}
